title: Two buyers, one seat: FOR UPDATE makes the second one wait
caption: The row lock serialises writers on that row only. The loser re-reads after the winner commits and sees the seat is gone.

messages.label: SELECT seat 12A FOR UPDATE
messages.note: A takes a row lock on seat 12A.

messages.label: SELECT seat 12A FOR UPDATE
messages.note: B asks for the same row lock and blocks. Other seats are not affected.

messages.label: UPDATE status = booked; COMMIT
messages.note: A books and commits; the lock is released.

messages.label: status = booked
messages.note: B wakes up and reads the committed row.

messages.label: ROLLBACK: sold out
messages.note: No double booking. Cost: hot rows queue, so 1 row at ~2 ms per transaction caps near 500 writes/s.

scenarios.name: Deadlock
scenarios.summary: Two transactions lock the same rows in opposite order and wait on each other; Postgres detects the cycle and aborts one.

messages.label: lock seat 12A
messages.note: A books a pair of seats: 12A first.

messages.label: lock seat 12B
messages.note: B books the same pair, but starts with 12B.

messages.label: lock seat 12A
messages.note: B waits for A: a cycle. Neither can ever proceed.

messages.label: ERROR: deadlock detected
messages.note: After deadlock_timeout (1 s) Postgres aborts one of them; A gets 12B and commits.

messages.label: retry
messages.note: Prevention: always lock rows in the same order (ORDER BY seat_id … FOR UPDATE), and retry on this error.

scenarios.name: Alternative: version
scenarios.summary: Optimistic concurrency: no lock is held; the UPDATE checks a version number and the loser sees 0 rows changed and retries.

messages.label: UPDATE … WHERE v = 7
messages.note: SET status = booked, v = 8. One row changed: A wins.

messages.label: UPDATE … WHERE v = 7
messages.note: 0 rows changed: the version moved on. B re-reads, sees booked and reports sold out. Best when conflicts are rare.

scenarios.name: Risk: slow call in lock
scenarios.summary: Holding a row lock across a slow external call makes every other buyer of that row queue behind it; keep the locked section short.

messages.label: call payment API (3 s)
messages.note: The lock is held the whole time.

messages.label: SELECT seat 12A FOR UPDATE
messages.note: B and everyone after it waits 3 s, holding connections from the pool too.

messages.label: status = booked
messages.note: Mitigation: reserve the seat with a short transaction (status = held, expires_at), pay outside any lock, then confirm. Set lock_timeout.
